newsitem.title: UK: Middle Eastern tanker rates firm amid solid fixing.
newsitem.headline: Middle Eastern tanker rates firm amid solid fixing.

text.p: Middle Eastern tanker chartering rates were slightly stronger on Tuesday amid steady fixing, brokers said.
"The market seems pretty firm. AG rates for Japan have ticked up a tad," one said.
Two VLCCs -- the Diamond Bell loading Oct 18 and the Nichiriyu loading Oct 24 -- were seen fixed at W57.5 for such trips against rates of W55 reported on Monday.
In the Mediterranean rates looked a little frayed at the edges after a very quiet day -- 80,000 tonners on cross-Med trips were put at W100, while 130,000 tonners were put at W85.
"It's very quiet we've hardly seen any activity at all," one trader said. There was talk BP had fixed two vessels -- out of Algeria and Banias, but this was not confirmed.
The inter UK-continental sector was fairly busy. A wide range of rates for cross sector trips by 80,000 tonners was reported from W100 to W106.25.

The Caribbean up U.S. coast market was a little softer with 70,000 tonners on such trips seen fixed at W130-135. "Basically there are quite a few vessels out there looking for work, which has slackened rates," one broker said.
